graders.run: uv run python -c "import flywheel_core; import flywheel_orchestrator"
graders.name: optional-extra-import-boundary

goal: Port the orchestrator cross-task read functions onto the backend-agnostic query surface and implement that surface on PostgresStore, so history-listing, live-rows, and latest-lifecycle/resolve_run_id reads return field-for-field-identical results on SQLite and Postgres for the same write-protocol-seeded state.

relevant: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_history.py -- _attempt_rollups, _select_lifecycles, _history_run_from_row, resolve_run_id, collect_run_detail all reach store._connection and are typed SqliteStore; retype off SqliteStore-only and route through the query-surface protocol. The history listing (collect_history_rows -> _select_lifecycles) must ENUMERATE terminal runs through list_lifecycles(statuses=TERMINAL_STATUSES) -- the existing (DONE, FAILED, FAILED_VALIDATION) tuple already named TERMINAL_STATUSES at _history.py:41 -- NOT a SQLite-only store._connection lifecycle SELECT (spec D-6). 00030's query-migrate-orchestrator-reads (a prerequisite) already rewrites this _select_lifecycles SELECT onto list_lifecycles on the SQLite side; this task makes that same call site work on Postgres by implementing list_lifecycles on PostgresStore.

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_workflow.py -- _latest_lifecycle_row (151), collect_live_rows (869), _list_blocked_lifecycles (1295) reach store._connection; task_state/status_rows_for_items/build_status_rows are typed SqliteStore; retype and route through the protocol

packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/store_postgres.py -- implement the query-surface protocol methods (list_lifecycles, summarize_spend, list_claims as the owning specs define them) here; psycopg already lives behind the TYPE_CHECKING/try-import boundary at line 47, keep it there
packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/store_sqlite.py -- the SqliteStore implementation of the same query surface is the parity baseline; mirror its result shape and ordering exactly
packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/store_protocols.py -- the LifecycleStore/query protocol the reads must call; do not add a new method name here (00030/00031 own the signatures)
packages/flywheel-core/tests/test_store_contract.py -- the backend-parametrized contract suite (memory/sqlite/postgres) that must stay green; keep it green
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_history.py -- existing SQLite history/show tests must stay green after the retype
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_workflow.py -- existing SQLite collect_live_rows/task_state tests must stay green after the retype
references: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_store_factory.py:142-168 -- the refusal these ports unblock; lifting it is a separate task (pg-factory-seam), not this one
.flywheel/holdout/00032-postgres-read-path-parity/ -- the held-out parity graders run against your committed change; they seed both backends through the write protocol and compare two computed reads
conftest.py:58-73 -- postgres_dsn / require_postgres session fixtures; the parity tests skip when no container is reachable
constraints: Consume the query-surface protocol owned by specs 00030 and 00031 VERBATIM -- list_lifecycles(self, *, statuses: Collection[Status] | None = None, task_id: str | None = None) -> list[Lifecycle] (SI-3); summarize_spend(self, *, since=None, until=None) -> SpendSummary (SI-4); list_claims(self) -> list[TaskClaim] (SI-10). Do not redefine, rename, or add to these signatures.
Implement these methods on PostgresStore so it satisfies the same read contract SqliteStore does; the SqliteStore read result is the parity baseline the held-out tests compare against.
Result ordering for list_lifecycles is (updated_at DESC, run_id DESC), identical on every backend, because latest-lifecycle-for-task depends on first-element order (SI-5).
Schema stays at CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 12 on both the SQLite and Postgres mirrors; author NO migration, add no column, no index, no version bump (SI-9).

The HistoryRow / HistoryRun / LiveRunRow (including the worker_id field that 00031 adds) / RunDetail / _latest_lifecycle_row tuple shapes must be unchanged -- the parity tests assert field-for-field equality across backends; do not add or drop a field.
Cross-task grouping and selection logic stays in the orchestrator functions; only the single-store SELECT primitives move behind the protocol (the orchestrator/core hard line).
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done; the worker verifies the committed end-state against the base it lands on.
non_goals: Do not modify, read, or author anything under .flywheel/holdout/00032-postgres-read-path-parity/ -- that is the held-out grading surface authored separately.
Do not modify files under packages/*/tests/ or weaken/delete any assertion; the existing SQLite suites are the must-not-regress floor.
Do not define, rename, or extend the query-surface protocol method signatures -- 00030/00031 own them; this task consumes and implements the fixed contract.
Do not lift the open_sqlite_bound_store refusal here -- that is pg-factory-seam, which depends on this task (refuse only after the reads are portable).
Do not add a top-level (module-level) import psycopg / import psycopg_pool to any module reachable from flywheel_core/__init__; keep psycopg behind the existing lazy boundary in store_postgres.py.
Do not bump CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION or author any migration.
edge_cases: The history listing must enumerate EXACTLY the terminal runs the store holds and no others: when the store holds two terminal runs plus a non-terminal (running) run, collect_history_rows on Postgres must return the two terminal run ids and omit the non-terminal one, matching SQLite (spec D-6). A left-behind store._connection lifecycle SELECT raises AttributeError on Postgres rather than enumerating, so it produces no complete terminal set and fails the history parity holdout; dropping the TERMINAL_STATUSES filter leaks the non-terminal run and also fails the exact-set assertion.

A task with multiple terminal runs of distinct update times must still resolve the most-recently-updated run as latest on Postgres (a no-op returning the first inserted row must fail the latest_lifecycle parity holdout).
live-rows must return rows only for in-flight runs (running/validating/awaiting_approval); a port that also returns terminal runs on Postgres fails the live_rows parity holdout.
Per-run rollup fields (tokens, cost, turns, iterations, attempt/iteration breadcrumb) must be populated on Postgres, not present-but-empty; field-for-field compare catches an empty row.
An attempt seeded with zero completed iterations must read back zeroed counters on Postgres, matching SQLite (a returned constant must fail).
notes: This task folds the core/store-postgres layer (PostgresStore query-method impl, layer-only on its own) into its consumer (the read-path port) so every change is graded by an observable parity behavior, not a layer-exists check.

psycopg is already imported behind the TYPE_CHECKING/try-import guard in store_postgres.py (line 47); flywheel_core.store_postgres is NOT imported by flywheel_core/__init__, so implementing methods there does not breach the optional-extra invariant.

CROSS-SPEC HARD EDGES (D-3 / D-5, wired by the reconciler): prerequisites are query-migrate-orchestrator-reads (00030 terminal -- transitively lands query-list-lifecycles-backends, the SI-3 list_lifecycles surface, AND migrates the _history.py/_workflow.py lifecycle reads off raw store._connection SQL FIRST, so this retype sits on the already-migrated list_lifecycles call sites instead of conflict-merging raw SQL in the same functions), agg-spend-summary (SI-4 summarize_spend + SpendSummary), agg-list-claims (SI-10 list_claims), and agg-worker-id-live-surface (SI-11 LiveRunRow.worker_id, asserted to cross to Postgres by the live-rows parity holdout). This task implements those fixed signatures VERBATIM on PostgresStore and adds no new method name; it cannot compile against any of them un-landed.
